topic: Möbius-null compliance envelope for three-factor perfect-complier effects. Fix randomized full-support assignment Z over all subsets of {A,B,C}, one-sided received bundle D=g(Z) subseteq Z, outcome exclusion Y=Y(D), and independence of Z from the WARP-rational response map g and all bundle outcomes. Let g*(z)=z have positive mass and sigma_t(g)=sum_{z superseteq t}(-1)^{|z|-|t|}1{g(z)=t}. Prove that the unique inclusion-maximal WARP class containing all eight coordinate-separable maps and outcome-nonrestrictively identifying all eight perfect-complier means is E3={g*} union {g:sigma_t(g)=0 for every t}; classify its exactly 29 maps, including 21 interactive maps, by a symbolic Möbius/choice argument. Identify each mean by the signed probability and outcome-moment transforms and all seven factorial effects by Walsh contrasts. For every rational h outside E3, construct two finite Bernoulli outcome/type laws with identical observed (Z,D,Y) law and a different target mean. Add joint influence functions and simultaneous Wald inference when the perfect-complier share is bounded below, plus Bonferroni-Fieller inversion for weak denominators, without claiming uniform vanishing-share adaptation. Consumer: factiv::iv_factorial and Blackwell–Pashley's New Haven perfect-complier factorial analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact enumeration of all 4096 one-sided response maps found 244 WARP-rational maps and confirmed a 29-map envelope with 21 interactive additions; a symbolic 28=1+9+18 classification and finite Bernoulli observational-equivalence construction cover all 215 excluded additions. An outside-envelope mixture can pass all eight probability diagnostics, so outcome-moment isolation and the full converse are essential. Current Goff, Blackwell–Pashley, Kormos–Lieli–Huber, and 2025–2026 citing work did not contain the classification; separate JASA supplement C was unavailable. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove symbolically that the full-offer-pair branch permits exactly four maps with the remaining factor unresponsive and two with it responsive, completing the behavioral classification independently of enumeration. EARLY KILL TEST: Retrieve JASA supplement C and test whether it already permits the six null types with no irrelevant coordinate and states the same maximal perfect-complier support class; an equivalent result kills novelty. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_mobius_null_compliance.md

open_problems.open_problem: Under one-sided bundle receipt and WARP with three binary factors, characterize the unique inclusion-maximal response-map class containing every coordinate-separable map that outcome-nonrestrictively identifies all eight perfect-complier potential-outcome means.

source_refs.claim: For two cross-randomized treatments, Proposition 4 obtains outcome-nonrestrictive complier-interaction identification under a WARP-restricted separable support, with the broader support search performed computationally.
source_refs.author: Leonard Goff

source_refs.claim: Point identification for general 2^K factorial experiments relies on treatment exclusion, which makes each factor's receipt depend only on its own assignment and rules out interactive compliance.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell and Nicole E. Pashley
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: With two factors, coordinated compliance and cross-defiance make the saturated-IV interaction combine treatment interaction with effect-heterogeneity terms.
source_refs.author: Máté Kormos, Robert P. Lieli, and Martin Huber

open_problems.why_unsolved: Goff supplies the general binary-combination criterion and a two-factor WARP application, but not a symbolic three-factor classification. Blackwell–Pashley cover arbitrary K only under coordinatewise treatment exclusion; their main text says supplement C gives a more complicated weighted interpretation under weaker exclusion and that interactions become much less clear. That supplement was not independently retrievable during this scan, so checking whether it already admits the six critical null types remains the required early kill test. Subject to that check, the concrete missing step is to reconcile WARP choice restrictions with simultaneous zero-Möbius conditions on the eight target incidences, especially in the full-offer-pair branch, and then prove necessity for every excluded rational type rather than relying on enumeration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient maximal-support characterization, an exact symbolic count and classification of the admissible WARP maps, signed identifying formulas for all eight means, and finite observational-equivalence witnesses for every excluded addition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from unrestricted outcome heterogeneity to necessary-and-sufficient selection restrictions and then to a factorial-complementarity application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: IV identification should tolerate arbitrary outcome heterogeneity -> finite response types turn identification into a binary-combination problem -> WARP gives the selection restrictions economic content -> characterize the largest rational three-factor support preserving every perfect-complier mean

method_exemplars.technique: Translate outcome-nonrestrictive identification into row-space and binary-combination conditions for treatment-state incidence matrices, then prove necessity through latent-law perturbations in an observational null space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The eight desired targets are finite-treatment counterfactual means conditional on a response type, exactly the objects covered by Goff's criterion.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate randomized assignment-cell outcome and uptake moments jointly and propagate their finite-population limit law through ratio and factorial-contrast transforms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once signed identification transforms are known, the new estimands consume the same randomized factorial cell moments as conventional perfect-complier effects.

method_exemplars.technique: Express latent-moment identification through membership in the range of an observable-to-latent linear operator and construct the corresponding generalized kappa moment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides an independent operator formulation against which the proposed Möbius recovery map and its converse can be checked.

open_problems.open_problem: When the maintained three-factor WARP class includes rational response maps outside the point-identifying envelope, derive sharp bounds for the eight perfect-complier means and their seven Walsh contrasts under bounded outcomes.

source_refs.claim: The paper bounds complier factorial effects under weaker noncompliance assumptions; its sharp linear-program calculations focus on the two-factor binary-outcome case.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell and Nicole E. Pashley

source_refs.claim: For a 2x2 design with coordinated compliance, the paper develops direct and indirect bounds after decomposing the IV interaction into a target interaction and heterogeneity terms.
source_refs.author: Máté Kormos, Robert P. Lieli, and Martin Huber

source_refs.claim: Failure of the binary-combination condition establishes nonidentification with unrestricted outcomes, but the paper does not calculate the remaining identified set.
source_refs.author: Leonard Goff

open_problems.why_unsolved: Failure of a Möbius-null condition proves that point identification is impossible but does not quantify what remains learnable. Existing factorial bounds either specialize to two factors or organize latent compliance through factorwise restrictions rather than the complete three-factor WARP response polytope. The first proof step must therefore encode all WARP-feasible response maps and couple their probabilities to type-specific bounded outcome moments across eight bundles; separately bounding factorwise complier groups cannot ensure compatibility with a single rational bundle-choice map.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-dimensional linear or linear-fractional program proved sharp for each perfect-complier mean and Walsh contrast under three-factor WARP, with analytic facets for important submodels and valid confidence regions for its bound endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates bounds as the response to substantively implausible treatment-exclusion assumptions and keeps the complier target explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Factorial-IV point identification uses strong first-stage exclusion -> cross-factor takeup is behaviorally plausible -> bounded outcomes preserve partial information -> compute sharp WARP-compatible regions for common perfect-complier targets

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize principal strata and bounded potential outcomes, impose observed-cell restrictions as linear constraints, and optimize the causal target to obtain sharp Balke–Pearl-style bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest factorial-noncompliance bounds construction; the new work replaces its two-factor compliance structure by the three-factor WARP polytope.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose a saturated-IV interaction into the desired local interaction and compliance-type heterogeneity terms, then bound the nuisance pieces under transparent auxiliary restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This offers an interpretable analytic route for selected Walsh effects alongside the general optimization formulation.

method_exemplars.technique: Plug randomized-cell empirical moments into the bound program and construct confidence intervals that account for estimation of partially identified endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed region is likewise a finite-dimensional function of factorial assignment-cell probabilities and outcome moments.

open_problems.open_problem: For each of the seven nonconstant Walsh contrasts in a three-factor experiment, characterize the inclusion-maximal WARP response-map classes that identify that perfect-complier factorial effect even when the eight component means are not all identified.

source_refs.claim: The outcome-nonrestrictive criterion is parameter-specific, and the paper's two-factor application studies local complementarity without first requiring identification of every latent mean.
source_refs.author: Leonard Goff

source_refs.claim: Multiple treatment-instrument pairs permit direct estimation of conditional and interaction effects among joint compliers in a two-factor voter-mobilization experiment.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: A 2^K design produces main, two-way, and higher-order complier factorial estimands, but the point-identification analysis maintains factor-specific treatment exclusion.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell and Nicole E. Pashley
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Identifying all eight component means is stronger than identifying a signed Walsh contrast: observationally invisible changes in several latent means may cancel in one contrast. The all-means envelope therefore does not establish maximality for any main effect, two-way interaction, or the three-way interaction individually. Goff demonstrates the parameter-specific logic for a two-factor complementarity target, but the missing three-factor step is to solve for each contrast vector in the relevant treatment-state row spaces rather than intersecting the eight mean-specific row spaces.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every nonempty S contained in {A,B,C}, a characterization of all inclusion-maximal WARP supports identifying the perfect-complier Walsh effect tau_S, signed observable formulas on each support, and counterexamples for every strict enlargement.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation begins with a substantive synergy question and explains why ordinary noncompliance methods cannot answer it before defining a multiple-IV interaction estimand.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific questions concern synergy or diminishing returns -> noncompliance obscures received-treatment interactions -> multiple instruments isolate a local interaction -> determine exactly which rational three-factor supports suffice for each Walsh contrast

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the binary-combination and row-space criterion directly to a contrast-valued target, then perturb latent outcome laws in observable null directions for the converse.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Goff's complementarity result shows how a contrast may be identified without first recovering every component mean.

method_exemplars.technique: Use orthogonal factorial contrast vectors, joint cell-moment estimation, and finite-population ratio inference for complier effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target objects are the same seven factorial contrasts, with only the admissible latent response support changed.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop joint design-based inference for the eight signed-transform perfect-complier means and seven Walsh effects under the three-factor identifying envelope, including simultaneous Wald coverage for shares bounded away from zero and simultaneous weak-denominator Fieller inversion.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives finite-population asymptotics and ratio-estimator test inversion for factorial-IV estimands under factor-specific treatment exclusion.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell and Nicole E. Pashley
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper develops nonparametric estimators and finite-population asymptotic distributions for a rich class of factorial and dynamic effects under imperfect compliance.
source_refs.author: Pedro Picchetti

source_refs.claim: Exact and almost-exact randomization inference produces IV confidence sets that may become unbounded under weak compliance, making weak identification explicit.
source_refs.author: Hyunseung Kang, Laura Peck, and Luke Keele
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing factorial-IV inference supplies the component CLTs and scalar ratio machinery, and Picchetti broadens finite-population inference under imperfect compliance, but the Möbius-null identification map creates a specific dependent vector: distinct signed numerators share the same estimated perfect-complier probability, and the seven Walsh effects are another linear transformation of those ratios. Scalar intervals do not automatically control simultaneous coverage. The required proof begins with a joint linearization of all signed cell transforms, then separates the denominator-bounded regime from multiple-test inversion when the common denominator is weak; it must avoid claiming uniform adaptation as that share vanishes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint influence-function representation and covariance estimator, a simultaneous Wald region with asymptotic family-wise coverage when the perfect-complier share is at least epsilon, and a Bonferroni- or max-test Fieller inversion theorem valid for weak common denominators.

writing_exemplar.why: It integrates factorial estimands, finite-population inference, weak-denominator test inversion, software, and the New Haven application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Factorial noncompliance creates several local causal estimands -> identification yields ratios of randomized cell contrasts -> weak denominators require dedicated inference -> extend that logic to the dependent vector generated by Möbius-null transforms

method_exemplars.technique: Stack randomized-cell outcome and receipt contrasts, invoke a finite-population multivariate CLT, and use delta-method or quadratic test inversion for ratio estimands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed estimators change the signed weights but retain the same factorial randomization and ratio structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nonparametric estimators of factorial effects under imperfect compliance and derive their finite-population distributions from assignment randomness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the newest nearby treatment of finite-population factorial inference when receipt does not perfectly follow assignment.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact or almost-exact randomization tests for adjusted outcomes so weak instruments produce appropriately unbounded confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the coverage-preserving weak-IV logic needed when the common perfect-complier denominator approaches zero.

open_problems.open_problem: If one or more of the eight assignment bundles is unavailable, characterize exactly which perfect-complier means or Walsh effects remain outcome-nonrestrictively identified under three-factor WARP and what minimal additional assignment support restores them.

source_refs.claim: Fractional and incomplete factorial designs address absent or infeasible treatment combinations, but the analysis concerns assignment effects rather than endogenous WARP-rational bundle receipt.
source_refs.author: Nicole E. Pashley and Marie-Abèle C. Bind

source_refs.claim: The factorial-IV identification formulas use the complete 2^K collection of randomized assignment-cell outcome and uptake moments.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell and Nicole E. Pashley
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The binary-combination characterization makes identification depend explicitly on finite instrument support, while the two-factor complementarity application retains all offer cells.
source_refs.author: Leonard Goff

open_problems.why_unsolved: Full Boolean Möbius inversion consumes all eight assignment cells; deleting an offer bundle removes observable-operator rows and aliases some Walsh contrasts. Fractional-factorial work characterizes assignment-effect aliasing but does not incorporate endogenous rational receipt, while existing factorial-IV and two-factor WARP applications retain full support. The first proof step must replace the full Möbius inverse by a restricted incidence operator and determine which perfect-complier target vectors lie in its row space uniformly over the allowed WARP response maps.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient rank or combinatorial criterion for identifying each perfect-complier mean and Walsh contrast from an arbitrary subset of offer cells, with explicit formulas, nonidentification witnesses, and a minimum-arm augmentation rule.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates incomplete support through resource constraints and unavailable treatment combinations, then states the resulting estimability problem transparently.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Full factorial designs may be infeasible -> fractional designs preserve selected contrasts but alias others -> noncompliance adds latent bundle choice -> determine which local causal targets survive incomplete offer support

method_exemplars.technique: Recompute treatment-state incidence row spaces after restricting instrument support and use latent-law null directions for the converse.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its necessary-and-sufficient criterion is indexed by finite instrument support and therefore applies naturally after deleting offer cells.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent estimable factorial effects through restricted design-matrix contrasts and derive design-based variance formulas accounting for aliasing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once a local target is identified, its signed observable transform lives on the same incomplete factorial design matrix.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate an identified local effect as a ratio of outcome and compliance contrasts and propagate joint randomized-cell uncertainty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The incomplete-support targets remain factorial-IV ratios whenever the restricted row-space criterion succeeds.

open_problems.open_problem: For arbitrary K, obtain a non-enumerative Boolean-lattice characterization and count of the maximal WARP response class that outcome-nonrestrictively identifies all 2^K perfect-complier means under one-sided bundle receipt.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives brute-force algorithms for finite instrument and treatment supports, notes rapid computational scaling, and develops the rational-choice factorial application only for two factors.
source_refs.author: Leonard Goff

source_refs.claim: The factorial-IV framework allows arbitrary K, but tractable point identification comes from restricting compliance strata to products of factor-specific types.
source_refs.author: Matthew Blackwell and Nicole E. Pashley
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Unordered monotonicity links discrete-choice restrictions to binary-matrix structure and counterfactual identification in finite mixtures.
source_refs.author: James J. Heckman and Rodrigo Pinto

open_problems.why_unsolved: Blackwell–Pashley obtain K-factor estimands under coordinate separability, while Goff supplies a general finite-support algorithm but no symbolic factorial classification and documents rapid computational scaling. A three-factor Möbius-null result would reveal Boolean-lattice structure, but arbitrary K is not a verbatim reapplication: one must characterize rational choice on every principal ideal of 2^[K] and reconcile Möbius constraints across exponentially many target bundles. The located general 2^K and discrete-mixture results do not give the maximal rational interactive class or its cardinality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient combinatorial characterization of WARP maps in the maximal all-means identifying class for every K, together with an exact count or recurrence, a constructive signed identification transform, and strict-enlargement nonidentification witnesses.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames exhaustive finite-support identification as revealing but computationally limited, naturally motivating a structural replacement for enumeration.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite IV models permit exhaustive response-type searches -> brute force reveals new identification but scales rapidly -> factorial bundle choice supplies Boolean structure -> derive an arbitrary-K symbolic classification

method_exemplars.technique: Use binary-matrix properties and revealed-preference restrictions to translate latent discrete-choice mixtures into counterfactual identifying equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The arbitrary-K problem requires precisely a bridge from rational choice restrictions to incidence-matrix rank and mixture identification.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the finite-support binary-combination criterion as the algebraic endpoint that the Boolean-lattice classification must satisfy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the necessary-and-sufficient outcome-nonrestrictive condition, leaving the factorial combinatorics unresolved.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the vector of randomized factorial cell moments and propagate its design-based limit law through the resulting ratio and contrast map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any arbitrary-K signed identification transform ultimately consumes the same 2^K randomized cell moments.

literature_map:
1. Imbens–Angrist (1994) and Angrist–Imbens–Rubin (1996) provide the binary-IV benchmark: monotone selection isolates complier effects without outcome homogeneity.
2. Dasgupta–Pillai–Rubin (2015, JRSSB) supplies the potential-outcome and Walsh-contrast language for 2^K factorial assignment effects.
3. Blackwell (2017, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2016.1246363) identifies two-treatment conditional and interaction effects among joint compliers, motivated by the New Haven experiment.
4. Blackwell–Pashley (2023, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2021.1978468) generalizes complier factorial estimands and inference to arbitrary K but assumes coordinate-specific receipt.
5. Its main text says supplement C weakens treatment exclusion only to a complicated weighted interpretation and that interaction interpretation becomes much less clear; supplement C was not independently retrieved here.
6. Goff (2026 revision, arXiv:2406.02835) gives the closest prior art: outcome-nonrestrictive identification is equivalent to binary-combination or row-space conditions.
7. Goff's two-factor WARP application establishes complier complementarity identification under the separable support and uses computational support searches; it does not classify three-factor WARP maps.
8. Heckman–Pinto (2018, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA13777) connects revealed preference, unordered monotonicity, binary matrices, and discrete-mixture identification.
9. Navjeevan–Pinto–Santos (2026, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA23174) provides a related operator-range identification criterion and generalized-kappa estimation strategy.
10. Kormos–Lieli–Huber (2025, JAE, DOI 10.1002/jae.3120; arXiv:2301.04876) shows that coordinated two-factor takeup confounds treatment interaction with effect heterogeneity and develops bounds.
11. Blackwell–Pashley (2026, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asaf084; arXiv:2407.12114) bounds complier factorial effects under weaker restrictions, with sharp computations centered on K=2 binary outcomes.
12. Pashley–Bind (2023, Canadian Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1002/cjs.11734; arXiv:1905.07596) studies fractional and incomplete factorial support but not endogenous WARP bundle receipt.
13. Picchetti (2026, arXiv:2601.16749) develops finite-population inference for factorial and panel effects under imperfect compliance, creating a close inference benchmark but not the Möbius support classification.
14. Kang–Peck–Keele (2018, JRSSA, DOI 10.1111/rssa.12353; arXiv:1606.04146) supplies weak-IV randomization-test inversion whose unbounded confidence sets reveal weak compliance.
15. The unresolved tension is that existing K-factor methods obtain clean effects by excluding interactive receipt, while rational-choice/outcome-nonrestrictive theory supplies the general algebra and a two-factor application but no located three-factor Möbius-null envelope, symbolic 29-map classification, or full converse.
